name: Kaioken Skillgen
summary: Kaioken/skillgen is a structural module that generates task-oriented skill documents for AI coding agents. It consists of a proposal stage that decides which skills to write based on repository evidence, a writing stage that produces grounded markdown checklists and verifies citations/commands, plus supporting tests.
keyPoints: Two-stage pipeline: proposeSkills() in src/propose.ts uses a plan prompt to pick 5-12 kebab-case, verb-led skill names and descriptions; writeSkill() in src/write.ts turns each proposal into a concise markdown guide grounded in real repository files.

Grounded documentation: the WRITE_SYSTEM prompt insists each step names real files/functions, shows verbatim excerpts with paths, and avoids restating what code is; buildCorrectionPrompt() repairs citations to files that don't exist (citedButMissing).

Verification validation: extractPrescribedCommands() pulls commands like npm, pytest, cargo from skill bodies, then validateVerificationCommands() checks they exist as actual files in the repo, so purported verification steps are real.
Skill existence and naming: skillExists() prevents overwriting existing skills; slug() converts proposal names into safe identifiers for file paths.

Deliberately task-focused: both prompts warn against producing architecture-overview or project-structure skills (those belong to the wiki) and against generic knowledge like 'how to write Go'; descriptions must name concrete triggers for when to load the skill.
Tested via src/test/skillgen.test.ts with a scriptedClient that mocks model replies and a scanOf helper mimicking repository scans.

entryPoints.name: proposeSkills
entryPoints.note: Entry point for the proposal stage: takes ProposeInput (evidence, chapters, notes, commands) and returns a list of SkillProposal objects.

entryPoints.name: writeSkill
entryPoints.note: Entry point for the writing stage: takes WriteSkillInput and returns a WrittenSkill markdown document, grounded in sources.

entryPoints.name: skillExists
entryPoints.note: Checks whether a named skill already exists in the repo root before writing.
